steps.what: Capture patient record facts and link verified evaluation results
Draft patient records from the verified encounter packet

loop.purpose: Turn clinician-supplied facts into an encounter note
loop.check: Check patient and encounter identifiers and have the audiologist compare all findings and treatment statements against supplied facts
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing facts or unresolved errors require manual documentation
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates and structured result links handle fixed fields; narrative organization requires language processing

steps.what: Verify evaluation details and save the patient record

tasks.design: Use native encounter templates and result links in the clinical record {OTHER}, with an assistant drafting narrative from verified facts. The audiologist reviews every clinical assertion and saves the exact final note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative documentation repeats facts already established during care.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical scribes support drafts followed by clinician validation.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong laterality, omitted uncertainty and invented normal findings can change care.
tasks.human_edge: The audiologist distinguishes observations from interpretation and owns the clinical record.

reach.learn: Preserve encounter identity and amendment history

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation records for clinician validation before record integration; this supports drafting capability, not audiology savings.
The proposed task split and savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: This baseline covers documentation only; examination, diagnosis and monitoring are excluded.

In s1 the audiologist produces patient and encounter identifiers, dated findings, laterality, units, source result references, decisions and unresolved issues; 35 hours include capture and identity checks. Unavailable results are documented manually rather than inferred.
Use native record templates before a narrative model; OTHER means clinical record system.
No diagnosis, treatment selection or autonomous record write is delegated.
research_questions: Does checked drafting save documentation time without changing laterality, uncertainty or treatment facts?

already_counted.description: Capture, draft correction and final note verification

incremental.description: Audit omissions and maintain documentation templates

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, encounter and final note text; any edit invalidates approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=89.5; gross 10.5 less 5 focal upkeep gives 5.5 central net. Report 0-2 until audiology documentation is timed; difficult notes may require full manual rewriting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate hearing and balance disorders and determine treatment

steps.what: Evaluate hearing and balance findings and determine diagnoses and treatment

tasks.design: Retain clinical evaluation and treatment decisions with the audiologist, consulting the clinical record {OTHER}. Documentation savings belong solely to the separate record-maintenance task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings must be interpreted in the patient's clinical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records provide context without automating diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing causes, managing uncertainty and selecting appropriate next care.
tasks.human_edge: The audiologist weighs conflicting evidence and explains the clinical decision.

reach.learn: Recognize when another clinical assessment is needed

evidence.claim: No audiology diagnostic automation is established by the provided digest; manual clinical reasoning is the proposed design.

assumptions: The baseline is clinical evaluation rather than note preparation or test administration.
Test findings come from the clinician conducting the separate assessment procedure; no free automated eligibility or diagnosis field is assumed.
OTHER means existing clinical record system; no new diagnostic service is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep follows from retaining the current clinical process.
unknowns: Clinical scope and existing diagnostic aids
research_questions: Does a measured repetitive calculation exist within this diagnostic task?

already_counted.description: Clinical evaluation and treatment reasoning remain fully counted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. No documentation saving is counted twice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor patients through ongoing observation of hearing and balance status

tasks.design: Keep patient observation and progress interpretation with the audiologist, using the clinical record {OTHER} for comparison. A chart may support that review, but it does not replace observation or create a separate saving here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress depends on symptoms, function and the reliability of measurements.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views allow comparison while the clinician observes the patient.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing genuine change from inconsistent responses and changing circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: The audiologist notices concerns that a numerical trend may conceal.

reach.task: Observe device use and patient response
reach.learn: Relate reported benefit to clinical observations

evidence.claim: Keeping ongoing clinical observation manual is an unmeasured design choice; the digest does not establish audiology monitoring savings.

assumptions: The baseline is observation rather than record transcription; documentation is assigned to record maintenance.
The audiologist obtains current observations during s1 with all time retained; prior findings are existing clinical records, not newly generated readiness flags.
OTHER means clinical record system; native record views precede any new dashboard.
No new monitoring service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Does assembling trend data take measurable time distinct from observing the patient?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. Documentation and diagnostic gains are excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Instruct patients and communication partners through demonstration, practice and feedback

tasks.design: Retain accessible instruction, demonstration and feedback with the audiologist. Reuse approved materials in {DOCS} without inventing a new handout-writing stage or reducing practice time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Successful instruction depends on comprehension and the communication setting.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approved materials can accompany human teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting practice to patients and their communication partners.
tasks.human_edge: The audiologist checks understanding directly and adjusts the teaching method.

evidence.claim: Human demonstration and feedback remain the proposed approach; no measured receptive-communication teaching saving is supplied.

assumptions: This task concerns instruction, not creating patient education publications.
Needs and preferences are elicited by the audiologist within s1 with all time retained.
Existing approved DOCS materials suffice before adding a generative tool.
No new content service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which existing teaching materials support practice without reducing comprehension checks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving; no unsupported handout-production baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical judgment and accessible patient communication
reach: Coordinate with medical records specialists on note integrity
Learn communication coaching methods from speech-language pathologists
role.ambitious_version: An audiologist who reduces repeated note preparation while preserving clinical reasoning and patient practice
